property_summary: For every non-empty _tos array, C.transfer(...) always completes successfully and returns true; the mutant returns false instead for the same inputs, so the return value differs (the reference's transfer returns true for all admissible inputs while the mutant can return false).
For every non-empty _tos array, C.transfer(...) returns true; the mutant returns false for the same inputs, so assert that calling transfer returns true for all admissible inputs.

For every non-empty _tos array, C.transfer(...) returns true (the reference always returns true for any admissible inputs), while the mutant returns false for the same inputs — so asserting that transfer returns true for all admissible inputs distinguishes the mutant.

For every call to transfer with a non-empty _tos array and any callee address, the reference C always returns (bool) true (i.e. the call succeeds and returns true); the mutant returns false for the same admissible inputs, so asserting that the call's returned bool is true distinguishes the mutant.

For any callee address that reverts when called, the reference contract's transfer(...) call (which uses caddress.call(...)) will continue and return true (call failure ignored) while the mutant using call{value:0}(...) changes EVM semantics causing the call to revert propagation in some contexts and thus can make transfer(...) behave differently; therefore the invariant is: calling transfer(...) always returns true (does not revert) for all inputs when the callee may revert — the buggy variant can fail for some inputs.

For any inputs, calling transfer(...) on the reference C always returns true (call completes without revert) even when the callee's fallback reverts; the mutant using call{value:0}(...) can cause transfer(...) to revert for some callee behaviours and inputs, violating that rule.

For all inputs (from, caddress, _tos, v) where at least one _tos entry exists and a callee's fallback is payable and reverts on receiving nonzero msg.value, the reference C never reverts and always returns true (i.e., transfer call completes); the mutant (which encodes the call with call{value:0}) can revert for some inputs when interacting with a malicious callee that distinguishes call vs call{value:0}, so the invariant 'transfer completes successfully' is violated by the mutant for some fuzzed inputs.

For every admissible input, calling C.transfer(...) never forwards any gas-dependent behavior to the callee that can change C's observable state or the success of the call loop — specifically, because the reference uses plain caddress.call(payload) (no explicit value or gas stipend), calls that revert are ignored and transfer always completes returning true; the mutant that changes to caddress.call{value:0}(...) changes call encoding semantics and can cause the overall transfer call to revert for some adversarial callee and inputs, so the invariant is that transfer(...) always returns true (does not revert) for all inputs in the reference but the mutant violates this for some inputs.

For any non-empty _tos and any callee, C.transfer(...) always returns true (does not revert) because the reference uses a plain low-level call whose failures are ignored; the mutant that changes the call to call{value:0}(...) can make transfer revert for some adversarial callee behavior and inputs, so the invariant 'transfer completes (returns true)' is broken by the mutant.

For every input, C.transfer never reverts and always returns true regardless of whether called external targets revert; the mutant that forwards all remaining gas allows a reverting callee to cause observable difference (call to transfer may revert or change behavior), so the property is broken for some inputs where the callee reverts.

For any inputs, calling C.transfer with any callee address and tos list never causes the external call to bubble up (the call is not allowed to revert the transfer call) — the reference swallows failures and always returns true; the mutant forwards all remaining gas allowing a malicious callee to consume/forward gas and cause the outer transfer call to fail or behave differently, so there exist inputs (a malicious callee and a tos entry) that make the mutant violate this property.

For any inputs, calling C.transfer(...) always returns (completes) and leaves address(c).balance unchanged (the reference swallows callee failures and does not have its own balance affected); the mutant that forwards all remaining gas allows a malicious callee to consume forwarded gas and cause the outer call to revert (or otherwise not complete) making the call fail — so the universal rule is that transfer never reverts (call succeeds) for all admissible inputs, which the mutant can violate for some adversarial callee.

For all inputs, C.transfer(...) always returns true (call completes) because it uses unchecked low-level calls that do not bubble up callee reverts; the mutant that forwards all remaining gas can allow a malicious callee to consume/forward gas and cause the outer transfer invocation to fail for some inputs, violating the universal return-true property.

For every input, C.transfer(...) always completes and returns true even if a callee reverts or consumes gas (because the reference uses an unchecked low-level call that does not forward extra gas), whereas the mutant that forwards gasleft() can let a malicious callee consume forwarded gas and make the outer call run out of gas and fail for some inputs.

For any inputs, calling transfer(...) never changes C's own state (calls to external caddress must not mutate C); replacing call with delegatecall can mutate C's state when the callee executes storage writes, so the mutant may change C's observable state while the reference never does.

For any inputs, calling C.transfer must NOT change C's storage (i.e., reading a public uint256 state slot remains unchanged); the delegatecall mutant can modify C's storage via the callee and thus violates this invariant for some inputs.

For all inputs, calling C.transfer(...) does not change C's contract balance (reference uses external call so funds go to callee; mutant delegatecalls into callee which cannot change C's balance but can execute payable code causing differences only in storage — however balance is unchanged for reference for all inputs while a malicious callee's fallback when invoked via delegatecall can make C send funds by using selfdestruct on itself; thus the invariant: address(c).balance is unchanged by transfer(), which reference preserves for all inputs but a delegatecall-based mutant can cause address(c).balance to decrease for some callee address and calldata.

For every input, calling C.transfer(...) never modifies C's own storage-visible uint256 variable named transfer (i.e., the autogenerated getter returns the same value before and after); replacing the external call with delegatecall can let a malicious callee mutate C's storage and thus break this invariant for some inputs.

For any inputs, calling C.transfer(...) never causes C to revert (the call returns successfully); replacing external call with delegatecall can make the interaction revert for some callee/inputs, so the mutant may cause transfer(...) to revert while the reference never does.
